data.title: National Energy Roundtable Conference Closes the Market
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Jason Langrish, President, The Energy Roundtable Limited ("The Energy Roundtable"), and members of The Energy Roundtable team joined David Chelich, Sector Head, Global Energy and Diversified Industries, Toronto Stock Exchange ("TSX") and TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV"), to close the market and celebrate the National Energy Roundtable Conference.

Founded in 2004, The Energy Roundtable is the private sector forum for defining the Canadian energy sector's role in domestic affairs and in global energy markets. Their policy roundtables and annual conference series in Toronto, Calgary, Houston and London gather energy sector leaders to advance the significant commercial opportunities that exist in Canadian energy.

The Energy Roundtable's market close takes place on the eve of the 11th annual National Energy Roundtable Conference. The event will gather six hundred leaders representing all aspects of the country's energy sectors for discussions on Canada's path to becoming a global energy superpower.

data.title: IC Group Holdings Inc. Named to the 2026 Deloitte Technology Fast 500
data.description:
Growth of 115% Driven by Recurring Revenue Expansion, Product-Market Fit of Core Solutions, and Growth Across All Three Business Segments.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - IC Group Holdings Inc.  today announced that it has been named to the Deloitte Technology Fast 500™, a ranking of the 500 fastest-growing tech companies in North America. IC Group grew 115% from 2022 to 2025.

IC Group's President & CEO, Duncan McCready, said, "Being named to the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 is a strong endorsement of the growth we've delivered across all three of our business segments. That growth is a result of the product-market fit of our core solution across our business lines, the trust we've built with Fortune 500 companies and professional sports teams to deliver consumer engagement at scale, and great customers who push us to innovate every day. These fundamentals will help us continue to grow into the future. We're well positioned to keep building on them. "

About the 2026 Deloitte Technology Fast 500

Now in its 32nd year, the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 provides a ranking of the fastest-growing tech companies - both public and private - in North America. Technology Fast 500 award winners are selected based on percentage fiscal year revenue growth from 2022 to 2025.

In order to be eligible for Technology Fast 500 recognition, companies must own proprietary intellectual property or proprietary technology that significantly contributes to the company's operating revenues. Companies must have base-year (fiscal year 2022) operating revenues of at least US$50,000, and current-year (fiscal year 2025) operating revenues of at least US$5 million, with a growth rate of 50% or greater. Additionally, companies must be in business for a minimum of four years and be headquartered within North America (United States and Canada).

About IC Group

IC Group is a consumer engagement company driving commerce and data for global brands and professional sports teams across live events, digital ecosystems, and mobile channels. Operating at the intersection of marketing, technology, and commerce, we simplify the complexities of modern consumer engagement for customers on a global scale.

data.title: Harmony Gold outlines mine safety actions after two fatalities this week
data.description:
Harmony Gold fell 7.3% on Wednesday after saying it is taking steps to improve safety at its operations following two fatalities at its South African mines this week.

Precious metals mining stocks fell across the board Wednesday as gold and silver prices plunged to their lowest levels in nearly 14 months.

Harmony said an employee, who had reported having been exposed to chemical fumes during acid treatment activities at the Mine Waste Solutions plant in Stilfontein during an incident on November 16, died in the hospital on November 17.

The incident occurred after an employee was killed while conducting tramming activities in the Carbon Leader Reef development section of the Mponeng mine in Gauteng on November 14.

In response, Harmony said it is sharing and applying the findings of both investigations across every operation; improving critical control verification to prevent loss of life at all workplaces; and strengthening ownership and accountability, assurance, hazard identification and workplace examinations throughout the group.

"Zero harm demands unwavering attention and accountability from every leader in Harmony," CEO Beyers Nel said.

data.title: HPE Adds Former JPMorgan Exec to Board, Amends Agreement With Elliott Investment
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Hewlett Packard Enterprise amended its cooperation agreement with Elliott Investment Management to allow it to add Jennifer Nason to the board.

The amendment allows HPE to have up to 15 directors on its board until its 2027 annual meeting. After the meeting, it will be limited to 13 directors, per HPE's filing Wednesday.

Nason most recently served as global chair of investment banking at JPMorgan until retiring in February 2025. In that role, she was a key adviser to HPE as the company evaluated its $14 billion acquisition of Juniper Networks.

In April 2025, activist Elliott Investment took a stake of more than $1.5 billion in the server and networking company. HPE signed a cooperation agreement with Elliott in July 2025.

This spring, HPE said it was adding Elliott partner Chris Hsu to its board pursuant to the agreement.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Anthropic IPO to mint thousands of millionaires
data.description:
Key points:
  • Early hires’ stock options are exercisable at less than $1 a share
  • Staff hold $119 billion in gains on paper
  • Company offered equity compensation for supporting roles

By Sabrina Valle

Anthropic's initial public offering is poised to create thousands of paper millionaires among current and former employees, in what could rank among the largest employee wealth windfalls in Silicon Valley history.

The offering is expected to unleash a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff who received stock grants as the Claude maker raced from startup to one of the world's most valuable companies.

The IPO filing shows the amount of wealth embedded in employee stock awards, but not how that wealth is distributed among workers. As a result, outside estimates vary widely.

Hill, a San Francisco marketplace for private-company shares, estimates 598 non-founder employees will hold at least $100 million in equity after the initial public offering, which is slated to open on the Nasdaq on Thursday at $83 a share, above its initial target range that would value the company at up to $1.4 trillion, according to a person familiar with the information.

Private-markets research firm Sacra estimates that roughly 2,800 current and former Anthropic employees could hold at least $1 million of pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation, the middle of the price range.

The firms say their estimates are model-based and use public information. Reuters could not independently verify the estimates, which reflect factors including vesting periods, exercises, tender transactions, option awards, restricted stock units, award timing, headcount and employee retention rates. The filing does not disclose sums due individuals.

But the wealth potentially shared by employees is vast. Anthropic option holders were sitting on $119 billion of paper gains as of September 30, at a weighted average exercise price of $2.91 per share, the company disclosed. About $73 billion of that amount had vested through service and could be exercised immediately.

Anthropic did not respond to a comment request on the estimates.

"The idea of equity appreciating to an amount that is life-changing is something that people strive for," Hill CEO Andrew Benson said. "It doesn't get better than this."

EQUITY AT ENTRY LEVEL

Workers who joined the firm when it started five years ago — even in administrative positions and entry-level jobs — could be sitting on life-changing wealth, reflecting their holdings of stock options that carry exercise prices of less than $1.

Options granted through 2023 and still outstanding at the end of that year carried an average exercise price of 52 cents, the filing shows.

At SpaceX , which was founded in 2002 and went public in June in a record-busting IPO, many of the employees who became millionaires had worked there for more than a decade.

"Early employees who started in a very junior role should have actually a better financial outcome than somebody who joined in a very senior role right before the IPO," Benson said, referring to Anthropic.

Non-founder Anthropic employees can sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first trading day, and up to another 35% after fiscal 2026 earnings.

EARLY HIRES REAP REWARDS

Founded in 2021, the Claude maker expanded its workforce rapidly alongside the AI boom, growing to about 5,300 employees as of September 30 from roughly 940 at the end of 2024. As it hired aggressively, the company used stock-based compensation as a key recruiting tool.

A May 2024 job posting for an administrative business partner role shows how the benefits of Anthropic's stock awards extended beyond AI researchers and engineers.

The position, which involved scheduling and managing calendars for company leaders, coordinating conference logistics and handling expense claims and reimbursements, paid an annual salary of $140,000 to $190,000.

The posting added that equity would be "a major component of the total compensation" beyond the salary, indicating that administrative and support staff were also eligible for stock awards alongside cash pay.

That year, Anthropic said it granted employees options at an average exercise price of $1.30 per share.

"And as we know from several anecdotes after the SpaceX IPO, this is often enough to help people down the organization chart do quite well in IPO," said Marcelo Ballve, head of research at Sacra.

Anthropic granted CFO Krishna Rao 14 million stock options in 2024, also with a $1.30 exercise price, according to the filing. At the IPO price range, those options would carry roughly $1 billion in gross intrinsic value, before exercise costs and taxes.

Ballve said that equity awards for administrative, support and entry-level roles are not uncommon at venture capital-backed companies. Historically, though, many companies phased out equity grants at hiring for these roles as they scaled up and salaries became more competitive, moving to performance- and tenure-based grants instead.

After Anthropic goes public, the company will likely reserve upfront equity grants solely for recruiting top talent, he said.

data.title: Enovix Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >ENVX
data.description:
Enovix Corp. (ENVX) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026.

As previously disclosed, on October 28, 2026, Enovix Corporation, a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), announced that the Board of Directors of the Company declared a distribution (the "Warrant Distribution") to the holders of record of the Company's common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the "Common Stock"), in the form of warrants to purchase shares of Common Stock (the "Warrants"). The Warrants were issued on the terms and conditions described in the Warrant Agreement (as defined below and attached as an exhibit hereto) and are being distributed on November 18, 2026, to the holders of record of Common Stock as of the close of business on November 13, 2026 (the "Record Date").

Pursuant to the terms of the Warrant Agreement, dated as of November 18, 2026, between the Company, Computershare Inc., a Delaware corporation, and its affiliate, Computershare Trust Company, N.A., as Warrant Agent (the "Warrant Agent") (such agreement, the "Warrant Agreement"), each holder of record of Common Stock as of the Record Date will receive one Warrant for every four shares of Common Stock (rounded down to the nearest whole number for any fractional Warrant). Holders ("other eligible recipients") of our 3.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 (the "2028 Notes") and the Company's 4.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 (collectively with the 2028 Notes, the "Convertible Notes") will also receive, at the same time and on the same terms as holders of Common Stock, Warrants without having to convert such other eligible recipient's Convertible Notes as if each such holder of Convertible Notes held a number of shares of Common Stock equal to the product of (i) the conversion rate applicable to the Convertible Notes in effect on the Record Date, and (ii) the aggregate principal amount (expressed in thousands) of Convertible Notes held by such noteholder on such date.

Each Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase, at the holder's sole and exclusive election, at an exercise price of $3.00 per Warrant (the "Warrant Exercise Price"), one share of Common Stock payable in cash. The Warrants may also be exercised, at the election of the holder, by delivery of certain issued and outstanding notes that may be designated by the Company from time to time pursuant to the terms of the Warrant Agreement (the "Designated Notes") by delivering an amount equal to $1,000 principal amount of Designated Notes to exercise up to 333 Warrants (subject to certain adjustments). The Company has initially designated the 2028 Notes as Designated Notes.

Unless the Early Expiration Price Condition (defined below) is met, the Warrants will expire and cease to be exercisable at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the date (the "Expiration Date") which is (i) April 28, 2028 or (ii) if the Early Expiration Price Condition occurs, the Early Expiration Date, where "Early Expiration Date" means either (x) the first Scheduled Trading Day (defined below) immediately following the Early Expiration Price Condition Date (defined below) (subject to the terms of the Warrant Agreement) (the "Scheduled Early Expiration Date") or (y) if the Company elects to set an Alternate Early Expiration Date (defined below), such Alternate Early Expiration Date.

Upon the occurrence of the first 30 consecutive Trading Day (defined below) period (the "Reference Period") that includes 20 Qualifying Trading Days (defined below) (whether or not consecutive) the first of which 20 Qualifying Trading Days must fall on or after the first Trading Day immediately following the distribution date of the Warrants (the "Early Expiration Price Condition", and the last of such 20 Qualifying Trading Days (whether or not consecutive) to occur, the "Early Expiration Price Condition Date"), the Expiration Date will automatically accelerate to the Scheduled Early Expiration Date, unless the Company sets an Alternate Early Expiration Date (defined below) in accordance with the provisions described below and as further described in the Warrant Agreement, in which case the Early Expiration Date will be such Alternate Early Expiration Date. In the event of an early expiration of the Warrants, Warrants will be exercisable until 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the Early Expiration Date. If the Early Expiration Price Condition occurs, the Company will make a public announcement by issuance of a press release to that effect as promptly as practicable after market close on the Early Expiration Price Condition Date setting forth the Early Expiration Date or an Alternate Early Expiration Date. Subject to applicable laws and regulations and the terms of the Warrant Agreement, including the occurrence of the Early Expiration Price Condition or the Additional Price Conditions (defined below), the Warrants may be exercised at any time starting on the date of issuance until 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the Expiration Date.

The Company may, in its sole discretion, elect to set the Early Expiration Date on a Scheduled Trading Day falling after the Scheduled Early Expiration Date (such date, an "Alternate Early Expiration Date"). In order to exercise the right to set an Alternate Early Expiration Date, the Company shall, no later than the fifth Qualifying Trading Day (whether or not consecutive) occurring in any 20 consecutive Trading Day period ending on or before the next following Early Expiration Price Condition Date (if any), make a public announcement by issuance of a press release that the Company is reserving the right to set an Alternate Early Expiration Date in the event the Early Expiration Price Condition does occur. If the Company sets an Alternate Early Expiration Date, the expiration of the Warrants on such Alternate Early Expiration Date shall be conditioned on (x) in respect of each of the two consecutive Scheduled Trading Days immediately preceding such Alternate Early Expiration Date, no Market Disruption Event (as defined in the Warrant Agreement) occurring and (y) the Daily VWAP (defined below) on each of such two consecutive Scheduled Trading Days immediately preceding such Alternate Early Expiration Date being at least equal to the quotient obtained by dividing the Warrant Exercise Price by the then-current Warrant Exercise Rate (as defined in the Warrant Agreement) (the "Additional Price Conditions"). As promptly as practicable after close on the Scheduled Trading Day immediately preceding the Alternate Early Expiration Date, the Company will make a public announcement by issuance of a press release as to whether the Additional Price Conditions are met. The Company may, in its sole discretion, postpone such Alternate Early Expiration Date to a new Alternate Early Expiration Date (which, for the avoidance of doubt, shall be conditional upon the Additional Price Conditions in respect of the Alternate Early Expiration Date so postponed). The Company may, in its sole discretion, postpone further (on one or more occasions) such Alternate Early Expiration Date of the Warrants to a new Alternate Early Expiration Date (which, for the avoidance of doubt, shall be conditional upon the Additional Price Conditions with respect to the Alternate Early Expiration Date as so postponed). The Company will make a public announcement of any such postponement by issuance of a press release as promptly as practicable after the close of regular market hours of Nasdaq on the Scheduled Trading Day immediately preceding the Alternate Early Expiration Date to be so postponed. If the Additional Price Conditions are not met as to an Alternate Early Expiration Date specified by the Company, unless the Company sets a new Alternate Early Expiration Date as set forth in the preceding paragraph (an "Alternate Early Expiration Date Annulment"), the Expiration Date will remain April 28, 2028 unless another Early Expiration Price Condition Date subsequently occurs. The definitions of Early Expiration Price Condition, Early Expiration Price Condition Date and Reference Period are subject to appropriate adjustment as set forth in the Warrant Agreement in the event of an Alternate Early Expiration Date Annulment.

All or any part of the Warrants may be exercised prior to 5:00 p.m. New York City time on the Expiration Date (as it may be adjusted) by delivering to the Warrant Agent a duly executed notice of election and the Warrants being exercised, and payment of the Warrant Exercise Price in cash or, if there are Designated Notes, by delivery of Designated Notes.

For the purposes of the foregoing, "Daily VWAP" of a share of Common Stock (or a Warrant or other security) on any date of determination means (i) in the case of a share of Common Stock, for any day on which trading in the Common Stock generally occurs on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (the "Exchange") (or, if the Common Stock is not listed on the Exchange, the U.S. national or regional securities exchange or association or over-the-counter market that is the primary market for the trading of the Common Stock on such day), the per-share volume-weighted average price in the consolidated tape system during regular market hours as displayed under the headings "Calculation: Bloomberg" and "VWAP" on Bloomberg page "ENVX US Equity AQR" (or its equivalent successor if such page or setting is not available) in respect of such day, (ii) in the case of a Warrant, for any day on which trading in the Warrant generally occurs on the Exchange (or, if the Warrant is not listed on the Exchange, the U.S. national or regional securities exchange or association or over-the-counter market that is the primary market for the trading of the Warrants on such day), the per-warrant volume-weighted average price in the consolidated tape system during regular market hours as displayed under the headings "Calculation: Bloomberg" and "VWAP" on Bloomberg page "ENVXW US Equity AQR" (or its equivalent successor if such page is not available) in respect of such day, and (iii) in the case of any other security, for any day on which trading in such security generally occurs on the Exchange (or, if the security is not listed on the Exchange, the U.S. national or regional securities exchange or association or over-the-counter market that is the primary market for the trading of such security on such day), the per-share volume-weighted average price in the consolidated tape system during regular market hours as displayed on Bloomberg page "AQR" for such security in respect of such day. If such information is not so available for the Common Stock or such Warrant or other security, the Daily VWAP on such date shall be the last reported sale price for the Common Stock or such Warrant or other security on such day.

A "Trading Day" for the purposes of the foregoing definition means a day on which the Common Stock (or Warrant or other security, as the case may be) (i) at the close of regular way trading (not including after-hours or extended market trading) is not suspended from trading on the Exchange or, if the Common Stock (or Warrant or such other security, as the case may be) is not listed on the Exchange, any U.S. national or regional securities exchange or association or over-the-counter market that is the primary market for the trading of the Common Stock (or Warrant or such other security, as the case may be) at the close of business, and (ii) has traded at least once regular way on the Exchange or, if the Common Stock (or Warrant or such other security, as the case may be) is not listed on the Exchange, such other U.S. national securities exchange or association or over-the-counter market that is the primary market for the trading of the Common Stock (or Warrant or such other security, as the case may be); provided that if the Common Stock (or Warrant or such other security, as the case may be) is not so listed or traded, "Trading Day" means a Business Day (as defined in the Warrant Agreement).

A "Qualifying Trading Day" for purposes of the foregoing means any S+W Trading Day (defined below) on which the Daily VWAP of the Common Stock on such Trading Day is at least equal to the Early Expiration Trigger Price (defined below) in effect on the last day of the Reference Period (subject to the conditions and limitations set forth in the Warrant Agreement). An "S+W Trading Day" means any day which is a Trading Day for both the Common Stock and the Warrants.

A "Scheduled Trading Day" means a day that is scheduled to be a Trading Day on the principal U.S. national or regional securities exchange on which the Common Stock is listed or, if the Common Stock is not then listed on a U.S. national or regional securities exchange, the principal market on which the Common Stock is admitted for trading. If the Common Stock is not so listed or admitted for trading, "Scheduled Trading Day" means a Business Day.

The "Early Expiration Trigger Price" is initially equal to $3.30, subject to certain adjustments.

data.title: Senegal parliament votes against 2027 budget bill, extending impasse
data.description:
Senegalese lawmakers have voted against a budget bill for 2027, National Assembly President Ousmane Sonko said on Wednesday, extending an impasse that threatens the West African nation's ability to secure a new lending programme from the International Monetary Fund.

Earlier this month lawmakers rejected an amended 2026 budget bill.

During a plenary session, a majority of lawmakers voted against the first part of the bill which included forecasts for revenues, debt and spending.

Sonko, who served as prime minister under President Bassirou Diomaye Faye until he was sacked in May, said it was therefore not necessary to hold a vote on the second part of the bill.

His Pastef political party controls the National Assembly and opposes the government's budget bills in their current form.

data.title: Perma-Pipe Announces Approximately $65 Million in Third Quarter Orders and Completes Majority Stake Acquisition in India
data.description:
Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. (), a global leader in engineered piping and corrosion protection solutions, today announced $37 million in additional new orders during the third quarter ended October 31, 2026. Together with the approximate $28 million in new orders reported in the Company October 20, 2026 update, third quarter total new orders total approximately $65 million.

Most of the additional new orders came from the MENA region, where demand for specialized pipeline solutions is supported by ongoing investments in oil and gas infrastructure and major energy-related projects, with the balance from North America. The additional bookings follow the Company's October 20, 2026 announcement of approximately $28 million in third-quarter bookings and reflect continued commercial momentum across its Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and North American (NA) regions.

In particular, MENA continues to represent an important growth market for Perma-Pipe. The Company's established regional presence, technical expertise, manufacturing capabilities and long-standing relationships with major customers and contractors position it to capitalize on opportunities arising from the region's ongoing energy infrastructure development. The Company's North American operations also contributed to the additional bookings, reinforcing the benefits of its geographical diversification and continued focus on expanding its presence across key markets.

Strategic Expansion into India

In a further milestone in its international expansion strategy, Perma-Pipe, through its subsidiary Perma-Pipe Qatar, has completed the acquisition of a 51% equity interest in the newly formed Welspun Special Coating Private Limited (WSCPL) from Welspun DI Pipes Limited (WDI), a wholly owned subsidiary of Welspun Corp Limited. WDI retains the remaining 49% interest.

The joint venture will focus on internal fusion-bonded epoxy (IFBE) coating and related activities in India. This acquisition expands Perma-Pipe's specialized coating capabilities and provides a platform to pursue opportunities in India's domestic market and international export markets, serving the oil and gas, water and industrial infrastructure sectors.

Saleh Sagr, President and Chief Executive Officer of Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc., commented:

“Securing an additional $37 million in bookings during the third quarter, bringing our total quarterly bookings to approximately $65 million, reflects the strength of our commercial momentum, particularly in the MENA oil and gas market. Our continued activity in North America further demonstrates the benefits of our geographical diversification.

“We are equally pleased to have completed the acquisition of a 51% interest in Welspun Special Coating Private Limited through Perma-Pipe Qatar. This partnership combines Perma-Pipe's specialized coating expertise with Welspun's established industrial presence in India, expanding our capabilities and providing an important platform to pursue opportunities in India and international markets.

“Together, these achievements reflect our commitment to disciplined expansion, strengthening our competitive position and creating new avenues for sustainable, profitable growth and long-term shareholder value.”

About Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc.

Perma-Pipe International Holdings, Inc. () is a global leader in engineered piping and corrosion protection solutions. The Company provides pre-insulated piping systems, leak detection systems, anti-corrosion coatings and related engineered products and services to customers across the energy, district energy, infrastructure, industrial, Oil & Gas, water transmission, and other critical infrastructure markets.

Perma-Pipe operates manufacturing and service facilities across North America, Middle East, North Africa, India and other strategic markets, enabling the Company to serve customers globally while providing local manufacturing and engineering capabilities.

For more information, visit www.permapipe.com.
